regenerate: python3 tools/detection-capture.py [--harness H] [--size COLUMNSxROWS] [--only PHASES] <dir> && cargo run -q -p muster-detect --example render_capture -- <dir> (prints the cases; scrub before committing)
why: herdr's own tests hold screens its authors typed; these are screens a real agent painted, at a named version, read the way the daemon will read them: the raw bytes Claude Code wrote to a 100x30 pseudo-terminal (or the size a case names), rendered by muster-vt, with the title from the terminal and progress from the OSC 9 scanner. Each case's expected state is what the agent was doing when the screen was taken - known from the script driving it - never this engine's verdict; a menu opened from the prompt is instead a screen to wait out, which leaves the state as it was, so a case failing after a manifest re-sync or a new agent version is the regression it exists to catch. Codex 0.154.0's screens were recorded the same way, read-only and asking before commands, with the same scrubbing. The first recording caught one: Claude Code 2.1.283 animates its title with half-circles, which herdr v0.8.0's bundled claude manifest read as idle. The capture directory's path (it held the recording machine's user name) is scrubbed to /tmp/capture, in the 2.1.288 plan cases too, where the recording machine's own statusline drew it, and in the menus the MCP servers' names, a home directory, an imported memory file's path and a hook's command are made generic; no rule reads them. Claude Code showed no folder-trust prompt, so that state is not here.
